item.description: Michelin is expanding its commercial tire distribution in the Philippines through BSB Junrose Corporation, which has been appointed as one of the tire maker’s new importer-distributors serving fleet and commercial transport operators. item.title: Green GSM drives change
item.description: Green GSM Philippines handed over 1,000 electric vehicles to driver partners during a three-day festival in Las Piñas City as the mobility company opened another route for drivers to enter the electric taxi business.

item.title: Behind every fast lap is a team
item.description: For a family: Discipline — and a team that believes in you — helps keep you on track. Zaf with Dad Atty. Alex Avisado Jr. and mom Christy Avisado.The roar of a kart engine can make racing look deceptively simple: a driver, a machine and a track.

item.title: GAC earns Kantar automotive recognition
item.description: GAC Philippines has been named the “2026 Breakthrough Brand — Automotive” in Kantar’s 2026 BrandZ Spotlight on Philippine Brands report, one of only two automotive brands recognized this year.

item.title: BAIC opens new dealership in Taguig hub
item.description: BAIC Philippines has opened a new dealership in Bonifacio Global City as the automaker continues to build its presence in Metro Manila.

item.title: VinFast builds Pasay base
item.description: VinFast Philippines has opened a dealership in Pasay City as it continues to add retail and service locations ahead of its target of 60 dealerships nationwide by the end of 2026.

item.title: Toyota GR opens karting to more families
item.description: Toyota Gazoo Racing has launched the GR KART in Japan as an entry-level racing kart for children and families who want a more practical way into motorsports.

item.title: VinFast, GSM appoint new global chiefs
item.description: VinFast and GSM have announced changes in their senior leadership as both companies continue their international expansion.

item.title: 10 Rare Indian Motorcycles And What They're Worth
item.description: The rarer the object, the higher the price. That's a good rule of thumb for many things, including Indian motorcycles from the first half of the 20th century.
